note: Role definitions as data: hats, not hardware. Any node may wear any hat the operator assigns; ceilings and expectations are this catalog's definitions, enforced by no running mesh yet (Part IV enforces at placement). SIMULATED paperwork in the same sense as the threat register: it proves the model's shape, not a live mesh.

roles.purpose: Hosts the Norns' orchestration duties: scheduling, routing and verification coordination for the whole mesh, including work of critical criticality that the mesh must not lose track of.
The human-facing door of the mesh: interfaces and command-line tools through which operators and callers submit, watch and cancel work, including critical work they remain answerable for.
Heavy-lift inference: the largest models and large-context reasoning the mesh can field, the hat a node wears when it is trusted with the deepest and most critical generation work.
Parallel code-generation workers: many hands producing code at once under the scheduler's direction, capped at standard criticality so critical work is placed on proven heavy hats.
The auditor's hat: invariant checking and verification of other nodes' work, which must itself be trusted at critical level because it stands guard over critical results (Part VI).
The skald's hat: vision work and naming — seeing images and giving things their words — generation in service of perception, capped at standard criticality in this catalog.
The cartographer's hat: mapping dependencies between models, tasks and knowledge, using embeddings to chart how the mesh's pieces relate, at up to standard criticality.
The scribe's hat: cold storage and the keeping of records the mesh may need again — provenance, history and archives — kept off the critical path, whose latency shape suits no urgency.
The emergency hat: fallback and overload handling when the mesh saturates, taking degraded emergency generation so that critical work is defended while casual work waits or is refused (Y-091).
